world.title: US measles cases reach 5,182 as elimination status faces review
world.summary: The United States has confirmed 5,182 measles cases in 2026, the highest annual total since 1991. State officials have reported at least eight related deaths, including deaths of young children. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the federal public health agency, has counted four deaths, leaving the
world.content: The United States has confirmed 5,182 measles cases in 2026, the highest annual total since 1991. State officials have reported at least eight related deaths, including deaths of young children. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the federal public health agency, has counted four deaths, leaving the national toll disputed. The case total is more than twice the 2,289 recorded in all of 2025. Officials and medical experts have linked the resurgence to falling vaccination coverage and distrust of health authorities. In the 2025-26 school year, 92.4% of kindergarteners received the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine, down from 95.2% in 2019-20. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s regional body for the Americas, is due to review U.S. measles-elimination status next week. The review will consider whether the virus has again established sustained transmission. The United States declared measles eliminated in 2000.
world.image_alt: US measles cases reach 5,182 as elimination status faces review

world.title: Democratic midterm wins trigger global sell-off in AI-linked stocks
world.summary: Global technology stocks plunged after Democratic gains in the U.S. midterm elections fueled fears of tighter rules and slower data-center construction. On Nov. 5, the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.36%, erasing about $2.53 trillion in market value. The sell-off spread to Asia on Friday, when Japan’s Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Ko
world.content: Global technology stocks plunged after Democratic gains in the U.S. midterm elections fueled fears of tighter rules and slower data-center construction. On Nov. 5, the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.36%, erasing about $2.53 trillion in market value. The sell-off spread to Asia on Friday, when Japan’s Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Kospi each fell about 6%, while European markets also declined. Investors reacted to campaign pledges to restrict data-center projects and doubts that heavy spending on AI infrastructure would produce returns quickly enough. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned for a halt to new data-center construction, while Democratic candidates elsewhere called for consumer protections and independent AI testing. U.S. shares recovered some of Thursday’s losses on Friday: the Nasdaq Composite closed up 1.1% and the S&P 500 gained 0.3% after employers added 165,000 jobs in October. Democrats are due to take control of Congress in January, when lawmakers are expected to pursue new AI and data-center legislation. International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said central banks should account for any slowdown in AI-driven growth.
world.image_alt: Democratic midterm wins trigger global sell-off in AI-linked stocks

world.title: London police investigate two new rape allegations against Russell Brand
world.summary: London police are investigating rape allegations from two more women against comedian and actor Russell Brand, who was convicted this week of rape and three sexual assaults. Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley said he would not be surprised if more women came forward. The Guardian reported that investigators s
world.content: London police are investigating rape allegations from two more women against comedian and actor Russell Brand, who was convicted this week of rape and three sexual assaults. Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley said he would not be surprised if more women came forward. The Guardian reported that investigators suspect there are at least 10 additional potential victims, though some information is second-hand and some women may be reluctant to report. The new cases add to a police inquiry that followed media allegations in 2023. Brand, 51, was found guilty on Nov. 5 of offences involving four women and acquitted of two rape charges and a charge of attempted indecent assault. He remains in custody awaiting sentencing on Monday, Nov. 9. The case has also prompted the British government to consider a proposal for judges to instruct juries on rape myths and misconceptions. The Metropolitan Police has sent files on the two new rape allegations to specialist prosecutors and is discussing them with the Crown Prosecution Service.
world.image_alt: London police investigate two new rape allegations against Russell Brand

world.title: Kenyan court sentences cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years
world.summary: A Kenyan court sentenced Paul Mackenzie, leader of the Good News International Church, to 200 years in prison on Nov. 6 for the murders of 191 people, including 190 children, in the Shakahola forest killings. The term consists of consecutive 100-year sentences for murder by starvation and direct homicide; 28 co-defenda
world.content: A Kenyan court sentenced Paul Mackenzie, leader of the Good News International Church, to 200 years in prison on Nov. 6 for the murders of 191 people, including 190 children, in the Shakahola forest killings. The term consists of consecutive 100-year sentences for murder by starvation and direct homicide; 28 co-defendants were also convicted and sentenced to prison. Prosecutors said Mackenzie ordered followers and their children to fast to reach heaven before the world ended. The court found that violence and confinement were used to enforce the orders; Mackenzie denied forcing anyone to starve, but the judge rejected his defense. Mackenzie’s lawyer, Lawrence Obonyo, said he would appeal. Those convicted have 14 days to file appeals. Mackenzie also faces separate proceedings linked to other deaths, including an allegation that he directed the deaths of 52 people at another site; he has pleaded not guilty in that case.
world.image_alt: Kenyan court sentences cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years

world.title: Protesters breach Microsoft data center site as European opposition spreads
world.summary: More than 100 protesters entered a construction site for a planned Microsoft data center in Amsterdam on Friday, Nov. 6, climbing a crane and setting off flares as demonstrators clashed with police. Dutch police said they detained 150 to 200 people suspected of trespassing and that one officer was slightly injured. Pur
world.content: More than 100 protesters entered a construction site for a planned Microsoft data center in Amsterdam on Friday, Nov. 6, climbing a crane and setting off flares as demonstrators clashed with police. Dutch police said they detained 150 to 200 people suspected of trespassing and that one officer was slightly injured. Pure Data Centres is developing the site for Microsoft, with plans for three towers and a capacity of 78 megawatts. The developer has said it intends to invest more than $1 billion. Protesters want large-scale construction paused until governments set clearer rules, citing electricity and water use, pressure on housing and climate goals, and the influence of technology companies. Microsoft says it supports peaceful protest but opposes unlawful or unsafe actions. The Amsterdam break-in occurred during two days of protests planned across Europe for Nov. 6-7. Campaigners also scheduled actions in countries including Ireland, Poland, Denmark, Finland, Spain, Italy, France and the United Kingdom. Technology companies argue that data centers are needed to support AI and cloud services.
world.image_alt: Protesters breach Microsoft data center site as European opposition spreads

world.title: US offers $20 million for intelligence on Iran nuclear program
world.summary: The United States is offering up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including facilities, equipment, personnel and their movements, U.S. Central Command said Friday. The State Department did not specify what information would qualify for the maximum reward. It said Iran
world.content: The United States is offering up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including facilities, equipment, personnel and their movements, U.S. Central Command said Friday. The State Department did not specify what information would qualify for the maximum reward. It said Iran’s failure to meet International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards obligations had left the agency without continuous knowledge of Iran’s production and inventory of key components such as centrifuges. The eight-month war began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Feb. 28, 2026. President Donald Trump has repeatedly said U.S. attacks effectively destroyed Iran’s nuclear program and that Tehran wants a deal. Earlier this week, he identified the suspected nuclear site known as Pickaxe Mountain among the targets he was still considering. Iran denies that the site is a nuclear facility. Mediators, including Qatar, are working to prevent fighting from resuming. Iran is reviewing proposals presented by Qatar, and Trump discussed de-escalation efforts with Qatar’s emir on Friday. No final agreement or Iranian commitment to nuclear concessions has been reported.
world.image_alt: US offers $20 million for intelligence on Iran nuclear program

world.title: Trump confirms limited Iran strike as Qatar-led nuclear talks continue
world.summary: President Donald Trump said U.S. forces carried out limited strikes Friday against an Iranian air-defense installation on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media reported two explosions near Suza; the semi-official Tasnim news agency said no official information on damage was available. Trump describe
world.content: President Donald Trump said U.S. forces carried out limited strikes Friday against an Iranian air-defense installation on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media reported two explosions near Suza; the semi-official Tasnim news agency said no official information on damage was available. Trump described the target as an anti-aircraft device and said U.S. forces destroyed it within minutes. The strikes followed Republicans’ loss of control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections, with voter dissatisfaction over the Iran war and higher fuel costs reported as factors. Trump has threatened further attacks while also saying negotiations are progressing. Qatari mediators have discussed a proposal under which the U.S. would lift its blockade and release some frozen Iranian funds in exchange for Iran allowing International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors access to bombed sites. Iran would then reopen the strait on the second day, with further talks addressing its nuclear program. Iran says it needs concrete U.S. steps before talks on its nuclear program; Trump says he will decide soon whether to strike again or pursue a deal. Fox News, citing U.S. officials, reported that Nov. 9 was under discussion as a possible date for renewed operations, but the U.S. military had not received an order to resume major combat.
world.image_alt: Trump confirms limited Iran strike as Qatar-led nuclear talks continue

world.title: Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay, urges unity and challenges euthanasia law
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Montevideo on Friday, opening a 12-day visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru with an appeal for cooperation and peace three weeks after surgery for lung cancer. In his first address, he urged Uruguayans to resolve differences through law, negotiation and patient agreement, and said people should
world.content: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Montevideo on Friday, opening a 12-day visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru with an appeal for cooperation and peace three weeks after surgery for lung cancer. In his first address, he urged Uruguayans to resolve differences through law, negotiation and patient agreement, and said people should receive care through the natural end of life—a challenge to Uruguay’s abortion and euthanasia laws. Uruguay, the pope’s first stop, formally separates church and state, and only 36% of its people identify as Catholic, according to a poll cited by Mercopress. Leo also said his experience as a patient strengthened his conviction that health care should be a right for everyone. On Saturday, Leo is scheduled to celebrate Mass in Paysandú, visit Montevideo’s Casavalle neighborhood, which is affected by violence and poverty, and lead a prayer vigil at Centenario Stadium. He plans to celebrate Mass in Florida on Sunday before traveling to Argentina; the tour’s final leg begins in Peru on Wednesday.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay, urges unity and challenges euthanasia law

business.title: Singapore Airlines details cabin upgrades ahead of S$2bn 2027 rollout
business.summary: Singapore Airlines has released more details of its S$2 billion long-haul cabin overhaul, adding specifics on economy and premium economy seating, cabin technology and airport lounges to its previously announced redesign across four travel classes. Economy seats will have 31 to 32 inches of legroom, while premium econo
business.content: Singapore Airlines has released more details of its S$2 billion long-haul cabin overhaul, adding specifics on economy and premium economy seating, cabin technology and airport lounges to its previously announced redesign across four travel classes. Economy seats will have 31 to 32 inches of legroom, while premium economy legroom will increase from 38 to 40 inches; both will get additional storage. The airline says research involving more than 5,000 frequent travellers, customers, staff and industry specialists informed the designs, with feedback emphasizing comfort, privacy and flexibility. The programme also includes 4K entertainment, updated food and beverage offerings, high-speed connectivity and lounge upgrades. Singapore Airlines plans to begin introducing the new cabins in the second half of 2027; it has not yet named the first routes to receive them.
business.image_alt: Singapore Airlines details cabin upgrades ahead of S$2bn 2027 rollout

business.title: IRS raises 2027 tax brackets and deductions to offset inflation
business.summary: The Internal Revenue Service raised federal income tax brackets and standard deductions for 2027, adjusting nearly 70 tax provisions for inflation. Taxpayers will use the figures on returns filed in 2028. The seven rates remain 10% to 37%, but higher income thresholds allow taxpayers to earn more before additional inco
business.content: The Internal Revenue Service raised federal income tax brackets and standard deductions for 2027, adjusting nearly 70 tax provisions for inflation. Taxpayers will use the figures on returns filed in 2028. The seven rates remain 10% to 37%, but higher income thresholds allow taxpayers to earn more before additional income falls into a higher bracket. The top 37% rate applies to income above $661,375 for single filers and $793,650 for couples filing jointly. The standard deduction will rise to $16,600 for single filers, $33,200 for joint filers and $24,925 for heads of household. The IRS adjustments are intended to limit “bracket creep,” which occurs when wage increases that merely keep pace with inflation push income into higher tax brackets. The adjustments do not guarantee a lower tax bill, which also depends on income, credits and filing circumstances.
business.image_alt: IRS raises 2027 tax brackets and deductions to offset inflation

business.title: US white-collar hiring rises in October as AI reshapes skills
business.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, while professional and business services — a broad category that includes legal, consulting and scientific services — added 70,000 positions. The sector’s gain far exceeded its monthly average of 15,000 over the previous year, but econ
business.content: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, while professional and business services — a broad category that includes legal, consulting and scientific services — added 70,000 positions. The sector’s gain far exceeded its monthly average of 15,000 over the previous year, but economists said one month of data cannot establish whether artificial intelligence is reducing or creating jobs. Economists quoted by Business Insider said AI is changing the skills employers seek, increasing demand for AI knowledge and critical thinking. The report does not isolate AI’s effects from other influences on employment. Indeed senior economist Cory Stahle said the sector remained below its long-term trend and cautioned against drawing conclusions from a single report. Temporary-help services added 18,600 jobs in October after losing 5,600 in September.
business.image_alt: US white-collar hiring rises in October as AI reshapes skills

business.title: Former OpenAI engineer pleads not guilty to office bugging charge
business.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer accused of hiding a recording device in an executive conference room, pleaded not guilty Friday in federal court in San Francisco. Prosecutors allege he placed the device behind a television on Sept. 28. He was arrested Oct. 9 and faces one count of intercepting oral commun
business.content: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer accused of hiding a recording device in an executive conference room, pleaded not guilty Friday in federal court in San Francisco. Prosecutors allege he placed the device behind a television on Sept. 28. He was arrested Oct. 9 and faces one count of intercepting oral communications, which carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine. He remains in custody after a judge found him a flight risk, and his next hearing is set for Nov. 17. OpenAI said it has no indication that customer data, source code or the model weights governing its systems were stolen. Prosecutors also allege Alfozan had frequent contact with an unnamed member of the Saudi royal family and received substantial foreign-government support. His lawyer, William Pernik, has challenged the allegations and said he will investigate the government’s evidence.
business.image_alt: Former OpenAI engineer pleads not guilty to office bugging charge

business.title: Canada loses 4,700 jobs as unemployment rises to 6.7%
business.summary: Canada lost 4,700 jobs in October and its unemployment rate rose to 6.7%, the highest in six months, marking a third consecutive monthly employment decline. Economists had expected a gain of 13,600 jobs and an unchanged jobless rate. The Canadian dollar fell 0.8% against the U.S. dollar Friday, leaving it down 1.1% for
business.content: Canada lost 4,700 jobs in October and its unemployment rate rose to 6.7%, the highest in six months, marking a third consecutive monthly employment decline. Economists had expected a gain of 13,600 jobs and an unchanged jobless rate. The Canadian dollar fell 0.8% against the U.S. dollar Friday, leaving it down 1.1% for the week, its steepest weekly decline since late September. Private-sector employment dropped by 53,000, while public-sector employment increased by 50,000. RSM Canada economist Tu Nguyen said uncertainty after Canada-U.S. trade talks stalled could be discouraging hiring and unemployment may continue rising through year-end. Nguyen said the weaker jobs market could lead the Bank of Canada to hold its policy rate at its December meeting rather than raise it again.
business.image_alt: Canada loses 4,700 jobs as unemployment rises to 6.7%

business.title: Ueno Bank collapse puts 1,000 Argentine tech workers on unpaid leave
business.summary: About 1,000 employees at Argentine technology company ITTI, part of the same business group as collapsed Paraguayan lender Ueno Bank, were suspended for 30 days without pay. South American football body CONMEBOL held about $13 million at the bank. Paraguay’s Senate removed President Santiago Peña on Friday over the ban
business.content: About 1,000 employees at Argentine technology company ITTI, part of the same business group as collapsed Paraguayan lender Ueno Bank, were suspended for 30 days without pay. South American football body CONMEBOL held about $13 million at the bank. Paraguay’s Senate removed President Santiago Peña on Friday over the bank’s failure, which left nearly 3 million customers unable to access their accounts. Regulators found that Ueno had lent $146 million to companies linked to its controlling shareholder, with inadequate collateral and records. After its accounts were corrected, the bank’s capital was less than half the legal minimum. Paraguay’s central bank has begun advance guarantee payments to some depositors, and prosecutors are investigating the bank’s collapse and the handling of public funds.
business.image_alt: Ueno Bank collapse puts 1,000 Argentine tech workers on unpaid leave

business.title: Fox completes $22 billion Roku takeover, expands streaming and advertising
business.summary: Fox Corp. completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku on Nov. 6, adding the streaming platform and its connected-TV business months ahead of the expected 2027 closing. Fox said the deal gives it access to Roku’s reach of more than 100 million households and brings the companies’ free, ad-supported services, The Roku
business.content: Fox Corp. completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku on Nov. 6, adding the streaming platform and its connected-TV business months ahead of the expected 2027 closing. Fox said the deal gives it access to Roku’s reach of more than 100 million households and brings the companies’ free, ad-supported services, The Roku Channel and Tubi, under a new unit called Fox Digital Platforms. The U.S. Justice Department closed its antitrust review after Fox agreed to carry competitors’ content on Roku for at least three years and not discriminate against rival media companies using the platform. Roku founder Anthony Wood joins Fox’s board and will co-chair the new division with Paul Cheesbrough; Mustafa Ozgen will lead Roku as CEO. Fox has also reorganized its streaming businesses, moving Tubi and Frndly TV into the portfolio led by Pete Distad.
business.image_alt: Fox completes $22 billion Roku takeover, expands streaming and advertising

business.title: Anthropic presses ahead with IPO as investors challenge $1.5 trillion valuation
business.summary: Anthropic is pressing ahead with a planned stock-market debut before the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday, but investors are questioning a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, and some have discussed figures closer to $1 trillion. Investors cited by the Financial Times said the company expects to raise $80 billion to $100 billi
business.content: Anthropic is pressing ahead with a planned stock-market debut before the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday, but investors are questioning a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, and some have discussed figures closer to $1 trillion. Investors cited by the Financial Times said the company expects to raise $80 billion to $100 billion at a valuation between $1.25 trillion and $1.75 trillion; its last private valuation was $965 billion. The pricing debate has intensified after a sharp technology sell-off, concerns about AI companies’ spending and election results that increased the prospect of limits on data-center construction. Anthropic reported about $17 billion in third-quarter revenue and plans to spend roughly $900 billion on computing and infrastructure, while holding close to $150 billion in cash and liquid investments, the Financial Times reported. Its roadshow is expected to begin next week, and JPMorgan plans an investor information session on November 13.
business.image_alt: Anthropic presses ahead with IPO as investors challenge $1.5 trillion valuation

science.title: MIT team uses flexible ligands to create new nanoparticle crystals
science.summary: Researchers led by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology used flexible polymer molecules to link gold nanoparticles into ordered crystal structures not previously observed, according to a study in Nature Materials. The team controlled nanoparticle assembly with flexible connectors rather than rigid ones. The team u
science.content: Researchers led by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology used flexible polymer molecules to link gold nanoparticles into ordered crystal structures not previously observed, according to a study in Nature Materials. The team controlled nanoparticle assembly with flexible connectors rather than rigid ones. The team used polyethylene glycol (PEG) chains carrying positive or negative charges. Experiments and computer simulations showed that the chains gathered where particles touched, limiting the number of links. The researchers said changing particle size and ligand length can also adjust the connections. The team has not yet tested the materials’ functions and next plans to try other particles and ligand combinations and test the resulting materials in practical settings.
science.image_alt: MIT team uses flexible ligands to create new nanoparticle crystals

science.title: Ancient Martian meteorite shows water altered crust 4.1 billion years ago
science.summary: Scientists say the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 preserves evidence that water altered the planet’s crust at least 4.1 billion years ago, near the beginning of Mars’ history. Discovered in Mali in 2022, the rock formed from mantle-derived magma and has a mineral and chemical composition unlike that of previously studie
science.content: Scientists say the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 preserves evidence that water altered the planet’s crust at least 4.1 billion years ago, near the beginning of Mars’ history. Discovered in Mali in 2022, the rock formed from mantle-derived magma and has a mineral and chemical composition unlike that of previously studied Martian samples. Researchers dated zircon crystals in the meteorite and used a laser-based rubidium-strontium method to confirm its age. By comparing its composition with observations of Mars, they identified 13 possible source locations in the planet’s southern highlands but have not pinpointed its origin. The findings were published in the journal Science on Oct. 29; scientists say further study of the sample could help determine how water shaped early Mars.
science.image_alt: Ancient Martian meteorite shows water altered crust 4.1 billion years ago

science.title: Higher BMI over time linked to faster cognitive decline in older adults
science.summary: A 24-year study of several thousand middle-aged and older Americans found that higher average body mass index (BMI) over time was associated with faster declines in memory and thinking. A team led by University of Georgia researcher Suhang Song reported the findings in the Journal of Neurology. The association was stro
science.content: A 24-year study of several thousand middle-aged and older Americans found that higher average body mass index (BMI) over time was associated with faster declines in memory and thinking. A team led by University of Georgia researcher Suhang Song reported the findings in the Journal of Neurology. The association was strongest when cognitive abilities were assessed about eight years after weight measurements and was more pronounced among participants who were older when the study began. The observational study cannot establish that higher weight causes cognitive decline or that weight loss would prevent it. The researchers noted that participants reported their own height and weight and that the analysis could not account for physical activity. The team called for further research into possible biological mechanisms and future interventions.
science.image_alt: Higher BMI over time linked to faster cognitive decline in older adults

science.title: AI identifies individual ovenbirds from songs with 96% accuracy
science.summary: Researchers used an artificial intelligence model to identify individual male ovenbirds from their songs with up to 96% accuracy in a test of Alberta recordings. The approach could help track which birds return to breeding territories without capturing and banding them, although it does not provide all the health infor
science.content: Researchers used an artificial intelligence model to identify individual male ovenbirds from their songs with up to 96% accuracy in a test of Alberta recordings. The approach could help track which birds return to breeding territories without capturing and banding them, although it does not provide all the health information that handling birds can reveal. In a separate account, animal-behavior professor Phil Starks describes hearing clicks near an acorn barnacle on Washington’s Olympic Peninsula. He says the observation did not prove the barnacle made the sound; synchronized video and audio could test the link.
science.image_alt: AI identifies individual ovenbirds from songs with 96% accuracy

science.title: Voyager 1 nears one-light-day milestone in November
science.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a distance of one light-day from Earth, a milestone the agency plans to mark Nov. 17. At that distance, a radio signal takes 24 hours each way, making the fastest possible exchange with the spacecraft a 48-hour round trip. The Leonid meteor shower is active through Nov. 30 and
science.content: NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a distance of one light-day from Earth, a milestone the agency plans to mark Nov. 17. At that distance, a radio signal takes 24 hours each way, making the fastest possible exchange with the spacecraft a 48-hour round trip. The Leonid meteor shower is active through Nov. 30 and is expected to peak overnight Nov. 17, with an estimated 10 to 15 meteors an hour. In the UK, cloud cover is expected to limit viewing in many areas this weekend, though forecasts indicate better viewing conditions in parts of southern and western England and Wales. The BBC says conditions may improve in more areas by Sunday night. Mars and Jupiter are due to appear close together before sunrise Nov. 15-16, and a full supermoon rises Nov. 24.
science.image_alt: Voyager 1 nears one-light-day milestone in November

science.title: Heatwave feedback can add 10% to extreme temperatures, study finds
science.summary: A study led by Yinglin Tian, a scientist at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, found that interactions among heat, dry soils and high atmospheric pressure can make the most extreme mid-latitude heatwaves about 10% hotter. High pressure brings more sunlight to the surface, while dry soils provide less ev
science.content: A study led by Yinglin Tian, a scientist at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, found that interactions among heat, dry soils and high atmospheric pressure can make the most extreme mid-latitude heatwaves about 10% hotter. High pressure brings more sunlight to the surface, while dry soils provide less evaporative cooling. In Central Europe, the threshold for this feedback is about 29°C; the chance of crossing it rose from 6% in 1979–83 to 23% in 2018–22. The researchers used machine learning and statistical analysis to identify the process, which they say current heat forecasting models do not represent well. A separate study led by Freie Universität Berlin researcher Philipp Aglas-Leitner compared 22 exceptional heatwaves from 2010–23 with projections through 2100. It found that future events could last longer and affect larger areas. For many regions, most model ensembles project at least one exceptional heatwave period a year in 2060–99.
science.image_alt: Heatwave feedback can add 10% to extreme temperatures, study finds

science.title: Researchers identify heme in 115-million-year-old Brazilian dinosaur fossil
science.summary: An international research team says it has found mineralized structures resembling red blood cells and heme, a molecule associated with hemoglobin, in a 115-million-year-old Aratasaurus museunacionali fossil from northeastern Brazil. The team describes the findings, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy
science.content: An international research team says it has found mineralized structures resembling red blood cells and heme, a molecule associated with hemoglobin, in a 115-million-year-old Aratasaurus museunacionali fossil from northeastern Brazil. The team describes the findings, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, as the first chemical confirmation of heme-derived molecules inside structures interpreted as dinosaur blood cells. The team says the structures lay inside the bone’s vascular canals and that the surrounding sediment lacked the same heme signature. It proposes that the mineral hausmannite helped preserve the structures and associated molecules; rapid burial in a low-oxygen setting may also have slowed decay. Paleontologist Mary Schweitzer, who was not involved in the study, disputes whether the evidence definitively identifies heme within the cell-like structures, noting that the chemical analysis covered the whole bone. The researchers say fossilization may have distorted the structures’ shape and that further work is needed to interpret it.
science.image_alt: Researchers identify heme in 115-million-year-old Brazilian dinosaur fossil

science.title: AI safety group finds Anthropic’s pace of benchmark progress nearly doubled
science.summary: An independent AI evaluation group, Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR), said Anthropic’s models were improving on clearly scored tasks in October 2026 at roughly twice their earlier pace. Its separate benchmark analysis estimated a 1.9-fold acceleration after October 2025, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.5
science.content: An independent AI evaluation group, Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR), said Anthropic’s models were improving on clearly scored tasks in October 2026 at roughly twice their earlier pace. Its separate benchmark analysis estimated a 1.9-fold acceleration after October 2025, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.5 to 2.8 times. METR said the result does not establish that the same acceleration applies to broader work or that superintelligence is imminent. METR judged that AI assistance now accounts for most of the acceleration, but said non-AI factors also contributed and that AI had not yet made highly significant, fully autonomous contributions to critical model-training work. Anthropic withheld much of the evidence METR considered most informative, limiting outside scrutiny. Anthropic co-founder Sam McCandlish defended the redactions, saying the details were commercially sensitive and could help other developers accelerate, while acknowledging that the omissions made the assessment harder to check.
science.image_alt: AI safety group finds Anthropic’s pace of benchmark progress nearly doubled

sports.title: Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis steps away to prioritize health
sports.summary: Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis says he is stepping away from basketball to focus on his health after his body failed to respond during preparations for the season. The 31-year-old has not played this season, and his statement did not say whether he plans to return or retire. Porziņģis signed a two-year
sports.content: Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis says he is stepping away from basketball to focus on his health after his body failed to respond during preparations for the season. The 31-year-old has not played this season, and his statement did not say whether he plans to return or retire. Porziņģis signed a two-year, $40 million deal with Golden State in June after joining the team in a February trade, but the Warriors have listed him as out indefinitely since late September. The team has withheld payments on his $20 million salary this season, and neither Porziņģis nor the players’ union is challenging the decision, according to reports. Golden State can still trade his contract, while Porziņģis says he wants to work with the team on a solution.
sports.image_alt: Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis steps away to prioritize health

sports.title: Ex-NFL receiver Antonio Brown avoids prison in Miami shooting plea deal
sports.summary: Former NFL wide receiver Antonio Brown pleaded guilty on Nov. 6 to aggravated assault with a firearm in connection with a 2025 shooting outside a celebrity boxing event in Miami. A judge sentenced him to three years of probation rather than prison, with conditions including weekly counseling and a ban on possessing fir
sports.content: Former NFL wide receiver Antonio Brown pleaded guilty on Nov. 6 to aggravated assault with a firearm in connection with a 2025 shooting outside a celebrity boxing event in Miami. A judge sentenced him to three years of probation rather than prison, with conditions including weekly counseling and a ban on possessing firearms. Brown had faced an attempted-murder charge after police said he took a gun from a security worker and fired two shots at Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu, whom he had fought earlier. Brown maintained he acted in self-defense. Prosecutor Howard Rosen said it was unclear whether Brown intended to shoot Nantambu, who was walking away, and that Nantambu did not want to pursue the case.

sports.content: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur said he met drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in São Paulo on Thursday evening after their first-lap clash at the Mexican Grand Prix. He said the team’s existing racing guidelines remain in place. He said the drivers must respect one another and put Ferrari, its employees and its supporters first. The Mexico incident cost Ferrari a chance at a one-two finish: Leclerc received a five-second penalty, while Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won; Hamilton finished second and Leclerc fourth. Qualifying for the São Paulo Grand Prix is scheduled for Saturday, with the race on Sunday. Ferrari is second in the constructors’ standings, and Mercedes needs to score three more points than Ferrari this weekend to clinch the championship.

sports.content: India dismissed New Zealand for 134 in 41 overs in the rain-shortened second one-day international in Wellington on Saturday, with fast bowler Gurnoor Brar taking 4-30. Set a target of 135 in a match reduced to 47 overs per side, India reached 39 for three after nine overs, having lost captain Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma early. Daryl Mitchell top-scored for New Zealand with 55 from 104 balls, while captain Mitchell Santner made 31. India’s other wicket-takers—Auqib Nabi, Anshul Kamboj and Axar Patel—claimed two apiece as the bowlers repeatedly found movement and bounce on a damp surface. India entered the match 1-0 up in the five-match series after winning the rain-affected opener in Auckland by five wickets. Rain delayed the start of the second match, reducing it to 47 overs per side. India now needs 96 more runs with seven wickets in hand to take a 2-0 lead.

sports.title: 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk’s reinstatement bid stalls over $13 million dispute
sports.summary: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk met with team officials in Santa Clara on Friday, Nov. 6, seeking a return to the NFL after more than two years away. Aiyuk said he is fully healthy, but the meeting, which included his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, ended without a resolution. Rosenhaus told reporters, “To b
sports.content: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk met with team officials in Santa Clara on Friday, Nov. 6, seeking a return to the NFL after more than two years away. Aiyuk said he is fully healthy, but the meeting, which included his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, ended without a resolution. Rosenhaus told reporters, “To be continued”. The NFL has told Aiyuk he must repay about $13 million in bonus money before it will reinstate him. The financial dispute involves the 49ers and the league’s management council. San Francisco voided about $27 million in future guarantees in 2025 after Aiyuk missed rehabilitation check-ins, then placed him on its reserve/left squad list. The 49ers still control his contract; a trade or release appears more likely than a return to the team, with the trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he had no role in the meeting and considers Aiyuk’s time with the team over.

sports.content: Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi says 18-year-old academy forward Luca Williams-Barnett is ready to start as Spurs visit Leeds United on Saturday, seeking a fourth consecutive Premier League win. Williams-Barnett made his debut with a brief appearance against Crystal Palace, and De Zerbi said he had considered starting him against Chelsea last month. Tottenham have won their last three league matches after going winless in their opening six. Midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur returns from suspension and defender Tosin Adarabioyo is available, while Lucas Bergvall, Savio and Mykhailo Mudryk remain out. De Zerbi has not confirmed whether right-back Pedro Porro will start after returning from a hamstring injury. The match kicks off at Elland Road at 12:30 GMT on Saturday, November 7; UK coverage is on TNT Sports 1 and HBO Max.

Extensive tests yielded results he called reassuring, but the cause remains unknown
sports.content: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson says he spent several days in the hospital after an unexpected medical emergency involving neurological symptoms that affected his strength, coordination and other physical functions. Extensive tests yielded results he called reassuring, but the cause remains unknown. He is working with specialists and physical therapists as he recovers. The 24-year-old has not practiced since being listed with an illness on Oct. 29 and missed New England’s 24-19 win over the Miami Dolphins on Nov. 1. He has been ruled out of Sunday’s game against the Green Bay Packers, and no timetable for his return has been announced. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said the team will support Henderson and his wife during his recovery, but said it was premature to discuss placing him on a long-term injured list. New England has Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back as it prepares for the Packers game.

sports.content: Seattle Seahawks guard Quenton Nelson will miss Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals ahead of a minor knee procedure. The team considers him week-to-week but will not place him on injured reserve. Seattle acquired Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts in a trade last week; coach Mike Macdonald said the knee issue predated the move and had worsened, prompting the team to address it now. Nelson is one of six Seattle starters ruled out, alongside quarterback Sam Darnold, left tackle Charles Cross, receiver Rashid Shaheed, defensive tackle Leonard Williams and edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu. Drew Lock will start at quarterback against Arizona despite managing an elbow injury in practice; the Seahawks also ruled out reserve defensive tackle Brandon Pili.
